title: An injury is a change to their one goal; "also want" on top is an add that waits
origin: Spec #9 (step log and next step), cases 4 and 6: the coach decides which a request is

history.text: Yo Leo! 2 miles around the park at 6:30. You in?

plan.reason: Four runs a week builds the base without wrecking your legs.

testerLines: bad news, rolled my ankle on the run yesterday. doctor says no running for 6 weeks

testerLines.say: could we do upper body stuff at home instead while it heals?
testerLines.means: asks to switch to upper-body workouts at home while the ankle heals
testerLines.when: after a ZOH text that doesn't ask him or her something else

testerLines.say: and separately I've been wanting to get my protein up too, like on top of the workouts
testerLines.means: also wants to raise protein, on top of the workouts
testerLines.when: after a ZOH text that doesn't ask him or her something else

facts: the ankle is sore but okay
you're not thrilled about no running
at home you have a yoga mat and a pull-up bar
6:30 in the evening still works for workouts
whatWentWrong: New case, not a past mistake: telling a change from an add.
shouldHaveHappened: The ankle is handled right away as a change to his one goal: sympathy without medical advice (pointing back to his doctor is fine), then work on an adjusted exercise plan (upper body at home) starts with him right away (asking what it needs, or showing it), never sent off to be thought about. The protein target on top is an add: a warm "let me think on it" with no promise and no nutrition questions or plan. ZOH never mentions a team, founders or approval.
